proposition.claim:
Equation reference: metric. For clarity this report writes \(v=\underline u\), \(r=|u|\), \(\mu=\mu^*\in(0,1)\), and \(k=\mu/(1-\mu)\). This \(v\) is not the separately rescaled coordinate \(v=4\underline u\) introduced on source p. 20. The field equations are \[\operatorname{Ric}_{\alpha\beta}=\partial_\alpha\phi\,\partial_\beta\phi,
 \qquad \Box_g\phi=0.\] The introductory gauge on p. 2 is \[
 g=-2\Omega^2(\mathrm du\otimes\mathrm dv+\mathrm dv\otimes\mathrm du)
 +h_{AB}(\mathrm d\theta^A-d^A\mathrm dv)(\mathrm d\theta^B-d^B\mathrm dv),\] with \(e_3=\Omega^{-1}\partial_u\), \(e_4=\Omega^{-1}(\partial_v+d^A\partial_A)\), and \(g(e_3,e_4)=-2\). The shift vanishes on the initial \(H_{-1}\). Equation (2.1), p. 14, prints \(d^A\mathrm du\) instead of \(d^A\mathrm dv\). This conflicts with the introduction and its displayed frame. The analysis of Problem 2 uses [metric] (#metric); its shift-free diagnostic is independent of this isolated coordinate discrepancy.

On \(v=0\), the prescribed spherical background has \[h=r^2\gamma_{\mathbb S^2},\quad
 \Omega_0^2=r^k,\quad
 \Omega^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\chi=\frac{2(1-\mu)}r,\quad
 \Omega\operatorname{tr}\underline\chi=-\frac2r,\quad
 \Omega\underline\omega=\frac{\mu}{4(1-\mu)r}.\] Theorem 1.1 combines weighted initial bounds through five angular and three outgoing derivatives, a small region \(v\le r\Omega_0^{2-\widetilde\delta}\), and an energy profile \[\int_0^v\left(|\widehat\chi|^2+
     |\Omega e_4\phi-(\Omega e_4\phi)_{\mathrm{corner}}|^2\right)\mathrm dv'
 =vf(\omega,v),\quad 0\le f\le1,\quad f\ge m>0
 \ \hbox{on a fixed ball }B_p(\epsilon).\] The parameter \(a\ge1\) is retained in later sections and may be set to one. Constants depending on fixed \(\mu,m,\epsilon\) are not uniform as \(\mu\to0,1\) or \(m,\epsilon\to0\). The elliptic unknowns are related by \[R=(va)^{1-\mu}e^{-(1-\mu)\widetilde\varphi}
   =(va)^{1-\mu}\psi^\lambda,\qquad
 \psi=e^{-\mu\widetilde\varphi}>0,\quad
 \lambda=\frac{1-\mu}{\mu}.\] The constructed MOTS is \(u=-R(\omega,v)\). Uniqueness proved in the elliptic argument uses the positive barrier and a priori bounded class. This review does not extend it to arbitrary uncontrolled graphs or to all notions of apparent horizon.

- pp. 1–13: all main theorem quantifiers; characteristic data; energy positivity; the degenerating \(C^0\) profile; hyperbolic/elliptic region matching and parameter dependence.

- pp. 14–24: metric/frame conventions; null structure and Bianchi systems; renormalized variables; derivative counts; initial norms; bootstrap smallness \(v a^{1/2}/(r\Omega^{3/2})\).

- pp. 66–74: MOTS equation, barrier direction, coordinate changes, natural quadratic gradient term, Moser and Schauder dependencies. The nested exponential in \(C(\kappa)\), (9.15), was retained.

- pp. 82–90: background cancellation in the instability proof; all-real amplitude quantifiers; \(C^0\) profile and intrinsic \(\dot H^{1/2}\) estimate; conformal free data and the full bibliography.

Theorem 1.3, pp. 4–5 (TeX lines 478–487), and Theorem 13.2, p. 84 (lines 5005–5032), prescribe the first component of the data as \[|\widehat\chi|(-1,v,\omega)=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i f_i(v,\omega)\] for arbitrary real \(\lambda_i,\lambda'_i\), not all zero, and assert injectivity of the pair of displayed initial-data components. The proof on pp. 84–85 chooses \(f_i\ge0\), supported on disjoint discs, with \(f_i\ge m_i a^{1/2}>0\) on a smaller ball. The \(C^0\) version on p. 87 replaces this lower bound by \(m_i g(v)^{1/2}a^{1/2}>0\) for every \(v>0\).

Proposition 12.4 and (12.5), p. 81, TeX lines 4851–4897, assert spacelikeness under the extra smallness condition on \(v\partial_v f\). After deriving \(R_v\ge (1-\mu)R/(2v)>0\), the proof prints \[g'_{AB}=h_{AB},\qquad g'_{Av}=2R_A,\qquad g'_{vv}=4R_v.\] These are not the pullback of the metric and frame specified on p. 2. The same paragraph also reverses the direction of a barrier bound.

The second estimate in Proposition 4.3, p. 30, repeated at the end of its proof on p. 31 (TeX lines 1837–1842 and 1916–1920), states \[\sum_{i\le4}\|r^i\nabla^i(\Omega\operatorname{tr}\chi)\|_{L^2(S_{u,v})}
 \lesssim \frac{va\,\mathcal O^2}{r}.\] The sum includes \(i=0\). At the prescribed \(v=0\) spherical data, with fixed \(r>0\), \[\Omega\operatorname{tr}\chi=2(1-\mu)r^{k-1},\qquad
 |S_{u,0}|=4\pi r^2,\] so \[\|\Omega\operatorname{tr}\chi\|_{L^2(S_{u,0})}
 =4\sqrt\pi(1-\mu)r^k>0.\] All higher angular derivatives of this background vanish. The asserted right-hand side is zero. The same failure persists in the one-sided limit \(v\downarrow0\) for admissible bounded-norm developments with this prescribed background. It is a test of the initial data used by the proposition, not a replacement spacetime or a parameter outside \(0<\mu<1\).

 \left[\frac14(D_3\operatorname{Ric}_{44}-D_4\operatorname{Ric}_{43})
          +\frac16e_4\operatorname{Scal}\right]h_{AB}.\] Here \(\alpha_{AB}=W(e_A,e_4,e_B,e_4)\) is trace-free. All its displayed vacuum terms are trace-free as well. The scalar coefficient in [badmatter] (#badmatter) does not vanish on all Einstein–massless-scalar solutions.
